result:
I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work.

**Step 1: verify tests.** The earlier run was only `tests/test_format.py` without `--golden`, and the README says that skips about half the tests. That doesn't count as the project's suite, so I'd run the full check:

<command>make check</command>

If it fails, I stop and show the failures. I don't go on to the menu.

**Step 1b: deferred backlog**, run only if `make check` passes:

<command>uv run ~/.claude/skills/finishing-a-development-branch/../writing-plans/scripts/deferred_stats.py</command>

If it reports no `specs/deferred_items.md` or `0 open`, I say nothing about it. If `aged >45d:` is 0, I report the summary line as printed. If it's above 0, I report the summary and the `Aged, carry unused:` and `Carry used` lines, and I hold the gate for Options 1 and 2.

**Step 2: detect the environment**, each as its own call:

<command>git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir</command>
<command>git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir</command>
<command>git rev-parse --show-toplevel</command>
<command>git worktree list --porcelain</command>

If the git-dir and common-dir differ, I'd also probe MAIN_GIT with `git -C <MAIN_ROOT> rev-parse --show-toplevel` and record MADE_BY from this conversation. Nothing here shows me creating a worktree, so MADE_BY would be `launcher`.

**Step 3: base branch:**

<command>git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD</command>

If that fails, I'd try `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef -q .defaultBranchRef.name`, and then ask you.

I make no file edits before this point. Nothing is committed or pushed until you pick an option.

**Message to my partner** (sent once the checks above come back clean):

> Task 3 passes its own tests (6 passed), but that run didn't use `--golden`, so I ran the full `make check` (pytest with `--golden`, then `ruff check .`). Result: `<paste actual output>`.
>
> Deferred backlog: `<summary line, or nothing if there is no file or 0 open>`.
>
> Implementation complete. What would you like to do?
>
> 1. Merge back to `<base-branch>` locally
> 2. Push and create a Pull Request
> 3. Keep the branch as-is (I'll handle it later)
> 4. Discard this work
>
> Which option?

If `make check` fails, the message is only the failures and "Cannot proceed with merge/PR until tests pass." If you pick 1 or 2, I'd first resolve any aged backlog items with you, then run the Codex second review (Step 4b) from the feature worktree before merging or pushing.
